hypotheses: The threshold t is strictly positive.
The threshold satisfies t <= rate when the rate is viewed as a real number.
conclusions: Under the natural-number-valued measure constructed from poissonPMF at the given rate, the real mass of all n satisfying |n-rate| >= t is at most 2*exp(-t^2/(4*rate)).
mathematical_definitions: The deviation event is {n in Nat : t <= |(n as a real)-rate|}.
The stated upper bound is 2 exp(-t^2/(4 rate)).
The measure in the conclusion is obtained by converting poissonPMF(rate) to a measure on Nat.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive nonnegative-real rate and every real t with 0 < t <= rate, the mass, under the natural-number measure obtained from the probability mass function named poissonPMF at that rate, of outcomes whose distance from the rate is at least t is at most twice exp(-t squared divided by four times the rate).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The rate must be strictly positive, so the zero-rate case is excluded and the denominator 4*rate is nonzero.
The threshold is restricted to 0 < t <= rate; no claim is made for t > rate or nonpositive t.
The event uses a non-strict inequality, so outcomes exactly t away from the rate are included.
The sample space is Nat and the center rate need not be an integer.
The conclusion is stated directly for a fixed measure on Nat, not for an arbitrary random variable on an arbitrary probability space having that law.
The conclusion uses Measure.real, converting an extended-nonnegative measure value to Real; finiteness is expected if poissonPMF is normalized, but that normalization is not exposed in the dossier.
ambiguities: The body of poissonMeasure only refers to poissonPMF(rate).toMeasure, while neither the point-mass formula nor the normalization of poissonPMF is supplied. Therefore the packet alone does not establish that this measure has the conventional Poisson distribution or mean equal to rate.

Because PMF.toMeasure and poissonPMF are outside the supplied dependency inventory, the exact semantics behind the real measure value cannot be independently reconstructed beyond the displayed conversion description.
